<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par152 />to follow with the sign of the accusative;<ref>According to De Lagarde, ''Novae psalterii graeci editionis specimen'', p. 26, {{GHGheb|text=יְשׁוּעָ֫תָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=3|verse=3}} is also an accusative after {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}}.</ref> but most probably we should read with the LXX {{GHGheb|text=שֻֽׁבְכֶם}} for {{GHGheb|text=אֶתְכֶם}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|o}}
(4) The fact that {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} (like {{GHGheb|text=אַ֫יִן}}) always includes the idea of a verb (''is not, was not'', &c.) led finally to such a predominance of the verbal element, that the original character of {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} as a construct state (but cf. i above) was forgotten, and accordingly it is very frequently separated from its noun (substantive or participle); especially so by the insertion of shorter words (of the nature of enclitics), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=6}}, {{GHGheb|text=לוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=11|verse=10}}, 12, {{GHGheb|text=לָהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=30}}, {{GHGheb|text=גַּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=14|verse=3}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=18|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=30}}; but cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=6|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=32|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, and {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} used absolutely in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=22|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=4|verse=4}}.—Hence, finally, even the transposition of {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} and its noun became possible, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=8}} and 41:15 {{GHGheb|text=וּפֹתֵר אֵין אֹתוֹ|translate=and an interpreter there is not of it}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=30|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=2|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=5|verse=17}} ({{GHGheb|text=וְאֵין}}=''neve sint''; cf. k above, on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=9}}); 30:27.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=5|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} is placed between the subject and predicate.

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|p}}
Rem. 1. Like {{GHGheb|text=לֹא... כֹּל}} or {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל... לֹא}} (see b above) so also {{GHGheb|text=אֵין כֹּל}} expresses an ''absolute'' negation, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=1|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=אֵין כָּל־חָדָשׁ|translate=there is no new thing}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=1|verse=4}} (cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אֵין מְא֫וּמָה|translate=there is nothing}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=18|verse=43}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=5|verse=13}}); as also {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־... אֵין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=2|verse=19}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=מְא֫וּמָה אֵין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=6}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|q}}
2. Undoubtedly akin to {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} in origin is the negative syllable {{GHGheb|text=אִי}} occurring in the two compounds {{GHGheb|text=אִי כָבוֹד}} (as a proper name, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=21}}; Baer {{GHGheb|text=אִֽי־כָבוֹד}}) and {{GHGheb|text=אִֽי־נָקִי|translate=not innocent}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=30}}; but the proper name {{GHGheb|text=אִֽיתָמָר}} is doubtful, and the fem. {{GHGheb|text=אִיזֶ֫בֶל}} very doubtful. In Ethiopic this {{GHGheb|text=אִי}} is the most common form of negation, prefixed even to verbs.

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|r}}
(''d'') {{GHGheb|text=טֶ֫רֶם|translate=not yet}}, when referring to past time is used, as a rule ({{GHGpar|107|c}}), with the imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל... טֶ֫רֶם|translate=none}}... ''yet''; see b and p above; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=45|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=3}}; with the imperfect in the sense of a present, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲטֶ֫רֶם תֵּדַע|translate=knowest thou not yet?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=30}}; but cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=15}}, and {{GHGheb|text=בְּטֶ֫רֶם}} with the perfect in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=90|verse=2}} (but see {{GHGpar|107|c}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=25}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|s}}
(''e'') {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫פֶס}} (prop. a substantive, ''cessation'') ''no longer'', including the verbal idea of ''existing'', cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=36}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=45|verse=6}}, 14, 46:9; used absolutely, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=6|verse=10}} in the question {{GHGheb|text=הַאֶ֫פֶס עוֹד אִישׁ|translate=is there none left?}} &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=9|verse=3}}; frequently also in the sense of ''non nisi''; with {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} paragogic ({{GHGpar|90|m}}) {{GHGheb|text=אַפְסִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=8}}, 10, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=2|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי וְאַפְסִי עוֹד|translate=I}} am, ''and there is none else''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|t}}
(''f'') {{GHGheb|text=בַּל}},<ref>Evidently from {{GHGheb|text=בָּלָה|translate=to waste away}}, from which stem also {{GHGheb|text=בְּלִי}} and {{GHGheb|text=בֶּ֫לֶת}} (whence {{GHGheb|text=בִּלְתִּי}} {{GHGpar|90|m}}), originally substantives, are formed.</ref> in poetic and prophetic style, and with a certain emphasis,={{GHGheb|text=לֹא}}, is used with the imperfect, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, 23 (immediately afterwards with a perfect); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=7|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=49|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=10|verse=30}} (but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=21}} before the jussive,={{GHGheb|text=אַל־}}); before an adjective, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=23}}; before a preposition, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=16|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=23|verse=7}}.

(''g'') {{GHGheb|text=בְּלִי}} with a perfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=6}}; with an imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=41|verse=18}}; to negative a participle, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=7|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=19|verse=4}}; to negative an adjective, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=1|verse=21}}.

(''h'') {{GHGheb|text=בִּלְתִּי}} to negative an adjective, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=26}}; on {{GHGheb|text=בִּלְתִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=3}}, see x; on<section end=par152 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
